title: Public issue tricks an agentic workflow into leaking private repository data
blast_radius: Private repository data reachable by the workflow's token, exposed through a workflow triggered by an unauthenticated third party.
summary: Researchers showed that a public issue containing crafted instructions could drive an agentic CI workflow into reading private repository content and surfacing it where the attacker could retrieve it. The pattern is the 2025 MCP injection a year on and one layer further into the toolchain: anyone who can file an issue can supply input to an agent that runs with repository credentials. Both the trigger and the credential are the problem; neither is fixed by improving the model.
containment: Guidance centres on restricting workflow token scope and refusing to let issue content select privileged actions.

sources.title: Public GitHub Issue Could Trick GitHub Agentic Workflows Into Leaking Private Repo Data

scenario.description: Attacker-supplied issue text selects privileged actions inside a CI workflow.
